finding.claim: Unauthenticated /fetch endpoint passes the `target` query parameter straight to http.Get with no validation, and returns the response body to the caller (full-read SSRF). An attacker can reach loopback services, internal networks, and cloud metadata (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/) and read the responses. Any scheme the Go client supports and any redirects are followed.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, response body echoed via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:22

trace.note: http.HandleFunc("/fetch", fetch) registers the route with no auth middleware
target taken directly from the query string
http.Get(target) issued with no scheme, host or IP checks
error text (err.Error()) is also returned to the caller, leaking connection details
upstream response body is copied back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check, private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, redirect restriction, or authentication on this path. The `allowed` map is only used by safeFetch, not by fetch. No middleware is registered; the default mux is used.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 passes the query param `target` directly to http.Get, main.go:22 echoes the body, main.go:41 registers /fetch on the default mux with no auth, and the `allowed` check exists only in safeFetch (main.go:27), not in fetch.
